absent: Architecture-specific static branch patching and jump entry update mechanics.
Delayed decrement worker behavior and timeout scheduling policy.
Full ftrace graph enter and return address retrieval with registers enabled.
Hardware latency and noise callback effects beyond entry and exit signaling.
Kernel register snapshot layout and function override consequences.
Module-aware address lookup and descriptor handling when modules are enabled.
Lock function classification rules beyond caller filtering use.

findings.text: Caller address helpers expose return addresses at successive call depths from zero upward, letting diagnostics attribute the current execution site.
Lock caller resolver walks outward a few frames and returns the first address outside lock functions, otherwise the deepest probed address.
Preempt trace hooks are disabled no-ops that accept two arguments and produce no effect.
Callsite section name selects either patchable function entries or mcount location storage depending on build configuration.
Trace core init is a no-effect placeholder when the corresponding feature is not compiled in.
Graph entry record carries the current function address plus a signed depth that permits negative checks, stored packed without padding.
Return address entry extends the graph entry with an extra saved return address field, also packed.
Graph return record carries function address, signed depth and an overrun counter for depth limit overflow, with an optional return value field, stored packed.
Graph callback types separate entry notification returning status from return notification, each receiving the corresponding record.
Graph operations bundle entry and return callbacks with a generic ops object, private data, saved entry callback and an index.
Return stack element stores return address, function address and pointer to the return slot, with an optional frame pointer for validation.
Graph enter wrapper forwards return address, function, frame pointer and slot pointer to the register-aware enter path with no register snapshot.
Graph tracing limits fix maximum return function depth at fifty and return stack allocation chunk at thirty two entries.
Graph liveness check reports dead state through an unlikely static branch on a global kill switch.
Unlikely and likely static branch selectors dispatch to architecture direct or jump helpers according to true or false key type and hint the result.
Fallback branch selectors without patching read the enabled counter and apply normal likely or unlikely hints, with a config-conditional selector.
Graph pause control uses an atomic counter on the current task, incrementing to pause and decrementing to resume, with a no-op fallback.
Task graph init, exit and idle init are empty hooks when function graph support is disabled.
Graph registration reports failure and unregistration does nothing in the disabled configuration.
Disabled graph return address resolution is the identity, returning the supplied return value unchanged.
Warning-triggered trace disable is an empty hook in this configuration.
Nonmaskable interrupt trace entry and exit forward true on entry and false on exit to hardware latency and noise callbacks when enabled.
Architecture trace register wrapper embeds a full kernel register snapshot.
Trace register accessors read or update instruction pointer, indexed arguments, return value, frame pointer, register offsets and function override.
Partial register sync either does nothing or copies instruction pointer and return value from a live register snapshot.
Maximum trace register argument count is six.
Static key stores an atomic enable count plus, when patching is available, a tagged union selecting type tag, jump entry list or module link.
Static key use before jump label init triggers a warning identifying the caller and key.
Jump entry stores code, target and key fields with helpers deriving absolute addresses either relative to entry fields or as direct values.
Jump entry flag helpers test branch versus count, test and set init state from low key bits, and report patch size.
Jump label type distinguishes no-operation patch from jump patch.
Jump type tags encode false, true, linked and mask values, with true and false branch helpers delegating to architecture test.
Static key initializers provide true and false starting states with matching enabled counts and type tags, defaulting to false.
Without patching, enable state is a plain counter where positive means enabled, with guarded increment, decrement, enable and disable transitions.
Without patching, label text reservation always reports free and label locking is empty, with cpuslocked aliases equal to normal ops.
Typed true and false key wrappers each embed a base key, with define and declare helpers for single, read-only, array and config-selected instances.
Enabled test validates the wrapper type and reports whether the counter is positive.
Static branch reference and power controls map increment, decrement and enable or disable requests onto the underlying slow key operations.
Deferred key extends a base or typed key with timeout and delayed work when rate limiting exists, otherwise it is only the key.
Deferred helpers define true or false rate limited keys, schedule delayed decrement, flush pending work, adjust rate and increment immediately.
Symbol name limit is five hundred twelve with a derived formatted symbol length accounting for name, addresses, module and build id.
Kernel address classifiers accept core text, core ranges or gate area, with symbol descriptors unwrapped directly or via module lookup under read guard.
Module address lookup reports absent and module descriptor dereference is identity in the non-module configuration.
Headers define unique inclusion sentinels for trace interrupt, trace register, jump label, rate limit and kallsyms interfaces.
